correctness.rationale: The quotient parametrization by three independent cubic sections is basepoint-free and birational onto a rational cubic. Its unique singularity is a node or cusp; the Wronskian condition detects non-immersion, hence a cusp. Distinct branch points force transversality of the quotient cubic to each coordinate axis wherever it is smooth, and exclude singularities at the other vertices. The square map is fourfold étale on the torus; at an axis node each of its two preimages has two smooth branches with exactly order-two contact, giving A3. The central vertex pulls back to A1. The biquadratic cover has eight tame order-two branch points, so RH gives genus 5 and total delta 5. This exhausts the basket. Tjurina sums follow from explicit ADE normal forms in char zero or at least seven. The exact verifier recomputes the seven-point distinctness of the cusp sample, H(Q1,Q2,phi)=0, its Wronskian gcd, cusp jet, central node, and two mod-31 comparison examples; script passed. Potential issue outside scope: characteristic 2,3,5 is not covered.

value.rationale: A published natural genus-five plane sextic family has only 3/5 multiplicity-two point counts known, while analytic type controls Jacobian/Tjurina invariants, adjacency, and singularity geometry. The complete A1/A2/A3 stratification identifies three genuinely distinct degeneration mechanisms, yields exact natural global Tjurina lengths 5,7,9 and produces an admissible four-cusp genus-five example. This is not a routine numerical substitution: identifying quotient cubics, their axis transversality, and the order-two branch contact makes a strict improvement over α≥4. No broader downstream theorem is asserted.
